objectives.textEn: Expand (a+b)^n for positive integer n; use summation notation.
Know the definition of e and the exponential series.
Understand y=e^x and y=ln x.
Solve problems with exponential/log functions: compound interest, population growth, radioactive decay.
Reduce y=k·a^x and y=k·[f(x)]^n to linear relations and read constants from slope/intercepts of a plotted line.
Intuitive concept of the limit; limit theorems (sum, product, quotient, composite; no proofs).
Find limits of algebraic, exponential and logarithmic functions.
Concept of the derivative from first principles; notations y', f'(x), dy/dx.
Derivative as the slope of the tangent at x=x0.
Sum, product, quotient and chain rules.
Derivatives of algebraic, exponential and logarithmic functions (incl. a^x, log_a x).
Concept and notation of the second derivative.
Find second derivatives; second derivative test and concavity.
Use differentiation for tangents, rates of change, and maximum/minimum problems (local and global extrema).
Concept of indefinite integration as reverse of differentiation.
Basic properties and formulae (k, x^n, 1/x, e^x); constant of integration.
Integrate algebraic and exponential functions with the basic formulae.
Integration by substitution.
Use indefinite integration to solve problems.
Concept of definite integral as a limit of sums of rectangle areas; dummy variables.
Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and properties of definite integrals.
Definite integrals of algebraic and exponential functions.
Definite integration by substitution.
Areas of plane figures by definite integration.
Solve problems using definite integration.

objectives.textEn: Apply the trapezoidal rule; decide over/under-estimate using the second derivative and concavity.

objectives.textEn: Concept of conditional probability.
Use Bayes' theorem on simple problems.
Concept of discrete random variables.

objectives.textEn: Discrete probability distributions as tables, graphs and formulae.
Expectation E(X) and variance Var(X): E(g(X)), E(aX+b), Var(aX+b)=a²Var(X), Var(X)=E(X²)-[E(X)]²; simple problems.
Concept and properties of the binomial distribution (Bernoulli distribution introduced; mean and variance, no proofs).
Compute binomial probabilities.
Concept and properties of the Poisson distribution (mean and variance, no proofs).
Compute Poisson probabilities.

objectives.textEn: Use binomial and Poisson distributions to solve problems.

Properties of the normal distribution (bell-shaped, symmetric, mean=median=mode, spread set by σ, total area 1).

Find x given a probability condition.
Use the normal distribution to solve problems.
Sample statistics vs population parameters.
Sampling distribution of the sample mean: E(X̄)=μ, Var(X̄)=σ²/n; N(μ,σ²/n) when X is normal.
Central Limit Theorem.
Point estimates: sample mean, sample variance s² (n-1 divisor), unbiased estimator.
